cards.title: IVIVE Systematic Underprediction of High Extraction Ratio Compounds
cards.claim: IVIVE predictions using the well-stirred model systematically underpredict hepatic clearance (CLH) for high extraction ratio (ER) compounds. While low ER compounds are frequently classified correctly as low ER (>90% accuracy), their numerical CLH predictions are often inaccurate (only ~25-40% within 2-fold). The majority of high ER compounds are misclassified as low or intermediate ER due to underprediction.
conditions: Applies to compounds where hepatic metabolism is the primary elimination route.
Based on analysis of human and rat hepatocyte/microsome data.
Assumes standard physiologically based scaling factors without empirical correction.
required_inputs: In vitro intrinsic clearance (CLint) from microsomes or hepatocytes.
Fraction unbound in blood (fu,B) and incubation (fu,inc).
Liver blood flow (QH) values (e.g., 20.7 ml/min/kg for human, 100 ml/min/kg for rat).
Observed in vivo CLH for validation.
limitations: The study uses known compounds; bias patterns do not determine the target drug's specific clearance.
Does not account for extra-hepatic metabolism or specific transporter effects not captured in the model.
High ER compounds have fewer data points in the dataset, potentially affecting statistical robustness for that range.
cards.downstream_use: Use this to qualify the reliability of IVIVE-derived CLH predictions. If the target drug is suspected to be high ER, expect underprediction and consider empirical scaling factors or alternative models (parallel tube/dispersion) with caution, noting that the source found no significant improvement with parallel tube models for human hepatocytes.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
